remaining_concerns: No admissible current-release model-card or certification artifact shows that current evaluation results are reflected in release documentation.
No admissible disclosure artifact shows that the developer-support migration subgroup weakness was actually disclosed in current release materials.
No approved mitigation, exception, or reviewed risk-acceptance record is in evidence for the subgroup regression.
The actor's narrowed caveated position is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new evidence satisfying the policy predicates.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor usefully narrowed the claim from an overbroad compliance position to a caveated one, but that refinement rests on the same admissible record and expressly concedes the key gaps identified in the initial audit. Under the policy text, certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On the evidence available to this role, aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support that certification may be arguable in principle, but they do not prove that the required current-release documentation or mitigation predicate has been satisfied. That distinction matters: a caveated rationale can describe what would be needed for compliant certification, but without the actual documentation or approved mitigation in evidence, present compliance remains unsubstantiated.
